summary: At 09:00 legacy-client invoice traffic was switched onto a newly enabled adapter configuration that omitted the region-header mapping the routing function requires; within two minutes invoice creation errors rose from under 0.2% to 38%, and 97% of sampled failures lacked that header. Datastore health stayed normal, and disabling the configuration at 09:19 restored the baseline error rate within three minutes, closing the causal loop. CPU elevation and an 08:54 PDF ticket are best read as a downstream symptom and an unrelated coincidence respectively. The decisive control point is configuration parity for required routing fields before a legacy path is enabled, not additional monitoring.

claims.statement: A newly enabled adapter configuration began carrying legacy-client invoice traffic at 09:00.
Invoice creation errors stepped from below 0.2% to 38% at 09:02, about two minutes after the routing change.
The legacy-client configuration omitted the region-header mapping that the modern-client configuration retained, so the two paths differed in exactly the field the router requires.
Requests on the failing path arrived without the region header: 97% of sampled failures lacked it.

Mechanism: the missing mapping produced requests the routing function could not resolve, and those unroutable requests failed invoice creation. The error rate is the symptom; the absent mapping is the cause.
The datastore was not a contributor: error rate, saturation and replication lag remained inside the prior week's normal range.
Application CPU moving from 51% to 65% is consistent with error-path and retry overhead rather than a cause; it is well short of exhaustion and no resource limit is evidenced.
Removing the configuration at 09:19 returned errors below 0.2% within three minutes, a rollback that confirms the configuration as the sufficient trigger.
Impact was scoped to the legacy-client path; the modern-client path kept the mapping and is not implicated by any evidence item.
The 08:54 PDF rendering ticket precedes the change and concerns a different function; no evidence links it to invoice creation failures.
Whatever review or validation preceded enablement did not catch a missing required field, since the configuration reached production traffic in that state.
About 3% of sampled failures did carry the header and are not explained by the primary mechanism.

relationships.basis: Enablement of a defective configuration implies no gate stopped it; the gate itself is not described.
Omitted mapping yields requests without the header.
The configuration only affects traffic once it carries legacy-client requests.
Sampled failure composition matches the proposed mechanism.
Unroutable requests are the intermediate step between the configuration defect and the observed error rate.
End-to-end contributor to outcome via C5.
Removing the contributor removed the outcome on the same timescale.
Eliminating the datastore alternative leaves the routing mechanism standing.
Path-scoped impact matches path-scoped configuration difference.
Error handling and retries plausibly raise CPU; direction is inferred, not measured.
A causal role for CPU cannot be excluded outright, only made unlikely by the rollback timing.
Temporal precedence without any mechanistic link; treated as coincidence.
Residual failures are unexplained by the header mechanism.
Disabling the configuration removes the defect and therefore the failure mode.

uncertainties.statement: Why the mapping was omitted (hand edit, template divergence, generation defect) is not evidenced, so recurrence risk cannot be sized.
uncertainties.impact: Limits confidence in any fix aimed at the authoring step.

uncertainties.statement: No evidence describes what pre-enablement validation, review or canary existed, so C11 is an inference from outcome alone.
uncertainties.impact: The upstream control point is proposed without direct support.

uncertainties.statement: The residual ~3% of sampled failures that carried the header have no explained cause.
uncertainties.impact: A second, smaller contributor cannot be ruled out.

uncertainties.statement: The direction of the CPU relationship is not established by measurement; only its implausibility as a primary cause is argued.
uncertainties.impact: Leaves a weak alternative branch open.

uncertainties.statement: Sampling method and population for the 97% figure are not described.
uncertainties.impact: The dominance of the header mechanism rests on an uncharacterized sample.

uncertainties.statement: Whether legacy clients are now served correctly by the prior configuration or are degraded in some other way after the 09:19 disable is not stated.
uncertainties.impact: Restoration of the error metric may not equal restoration of function.

uncertainties.statement: Nothing indicates whether failed invoice creations were lost, queued or retried successfully.
uncertainties.impact: Business impact and any needed reconciliation are unknown.

uncertainties.statement: The PDF ticket is dismissed on timing and domain separation only; no evidence affirmatively excludes a shared cause.
uncertainties.impact: Small chance of a missed common factor.

actions.statement: Keep the legacy-client adapter configuration disabled until the region-header mapping is present, and treat re-enablement as gated on that mapping.
actions.rationale: Directly removes the confirmed contributor; the rollback already demonstrates the effect.

actions.statement: Enforce a parity check across adapter configurations for every field the routing function requires, evaluated before a configuration can take traffic.
actions.rationale: Attacks the class of defect, not this instance; rests on the inferred gap in validation.

actions.statement: Make the routing function reject or flag a configuration that cannot supply a required field at load time, rather than failing per request in production.
actions.rationale: Moves detection ahead of customer impact; the router's actual failure semantics are not evidenced, so feasibility is unconfirmed.

actions.statement: Introduce a bounded rollout for adapter configuration changes so a defective configuration reaches a small fraction of traffic.
actions.rationale: Would have cut the 38% peak to a fraction of it; does not prevent the defect.

actions.statement: Tie an automatic alert on a step change in invoice error rate to recent configuration-change events.
actions.rationale: Shortens the 19-minute exposure but cannot prevent the failure; do not treat as a fix.

actions.statement: Investigate the ~3% of failures that carried the header before closing the case.
actions.rationale: Resolves the open branch that could hide a second contributor.

counterfactuals.statement: Had the legacy configuration carried the region-header mapping, the error step would not have occurred.
counterfactuals.assessment: Supported: the modern path kept the mapping and is unimplicated, and removing the defective configuration restored baseline.

counterfactuals.statement: If the datastore had been the cause, disabling an application-side configuration would not have cleared errors in three minutes and datastore metrics would have deviated.
counterfactuals.assessment: Neither occurred, so this alternative is rejected.

counterfactuals.statement: If CPU pressure had been the cause, recovery would have tracked load relief rather than the configuration change, and 65% would have to be a limiting level.
counterfactuals.assessment: Recovery tracked the configuration change and 65% is not evidenced as limiting, so CPU is treated as a symptom.

counterfactuals.statement: If the PDF defect were causal, errors would have risen near 08:54 rather than at 09:02.
counterfactuals.assessment: Onset aligns with the 09:00 change, not the ticket, so the ticket is set aside.

counterfactuals.statement: If only detection had been improved and the configuration left unchanged, the 38% failure rate would still have occurred, merely for a shorter window.
counterfactuals.assessment: Holds, which is why monitoring is classified as visibility rather than leverage.

counterfactuals.statement: If the residual 3% had an independent ongoing cause, the error rate would have settled above the prior baseline after rollback.
counterfactuals.assessment: It returned below 0.2%, so the residual is more likely baseline noise than a persistent second contributor, though this is not conclusive.
